title: CSV rerun Queue ownership cleanup
summary: Cleaned up stale Launch-specific CSV rerun ownership after the workflow moved to Queue. Launch no longer owns the CSV rerun tab, start request collection, or rerun command-history surface; Queue owns the CSV Rerun controls, DOM IDs, request collector, route ownership docs, and WebView/static coverage while continuing to call the dedicated /api/rerun/* backend routes.
reason: CSV rerun is now a Queue-owned audit-remediation workflow, but stale Launch labels, inventories, and tests made the repository look like Launch still owned the workflow. This cleanup aligns docs, DOM/global export inventories, request-collector placement, and tests without changing media behavior or backend rerun policy.
behavior_before: CSV rerun controls had transitional Launch-specific names, request collection still lived in a Launch-owned module, some route/test/docs wording associated rerun start/readiness with Launch, and WebView inventories did not reflect the Queue-owned rerun workflow namespace.
behavior_after: CSV rerun is presented as Queue > CSV Rerun in UI/docs/tests. Launch keeps only normal pipeline launch behavior and active-work controls; Queue owns CSV rerun request collection and DOM/control surfaces while /api/rerun/* remains the backend execution path and /api/pipeline/start is not used for rerun rows.
manual_validation: rg stale Launch CSV rerun ownership scan excluding archive/generated/changelog/release - passed; only expected Queue-owned/readiness/assertion references remain
rollback_plan: Revert the WebView cleanup files, inventory/doc updates, and tests in this packet. Because this phase does not change backend media policy or PowerShell execution behavior, rollback is limited to restoring the previous Launch/Queue UI ownership wording and request-collector placement.
